self_critique:
The end card is now close to a premium toy-commercial poster. Inflated candy letters sit in true palette hues (within 6 degrees), with deeper pillows and juicy clear-coat highlights. The cove reflects them softly, and a radial sunburst of single lavender shadows leads the eye into the word. The calm band reads clearly as four chapter clips (S01 day, S02 heart, S03 gummy, S04 Seurat), and the orb carries the same S01 bloom across the S04 circle-match cut, within 1 px.

The superposition story finally reads. During the roll every letter throws coloured streaks (yellow, pink, cyan, violet) toward the camera. On the bar-15 downbeat the three lights reach O, W pops from inside, the streaks snap to one shadow per letter and the word pulses. The split now peels out of the white orb instead of teleporting, and the hold has quiet beat accents.

What is still weak, bluntly:
- The fans are pastel beyond the first ~100 px. The lavender floor albedo and the key falloff wash them out, so the end letters' three-colour separation is muddier than the centre letters'.
- By luminance the wall is still brighter than the title. I chose G2's pastel ground over the critic's luma rule.
- The coloured orbs are still fairly flat discs on the bright ground. G1 rules out the critic's glow shell.
- There is a one-frame tri-colour stack at f59.
- The lower quarter of the frame is a quiet lilac falloff with faint streaks rather than something rich.

A further round would try a lighter, more neutral floor tint under the fans, a slightly closer or larger key so the colour carries further, and a limb-brightened halo shared with S04 so the orbs read as glowing lights.
measurements: Lighting balance chosen from 12 preview variants (renders/work/s05_title/v_*). Without the WallWash the backdrop read dusky; at 400 W it killed the fans. Raising the key from 360 to 560 W and lowering the wash from 260 to 200 W took the f52 floor-strip share of S>0.3 pixels from 11% to 18%.

Fan geometry: with the key at y 1.4 / z 1.05 (the critic's family) the fans were only ~40 px tall; at y 2.0 / z 0.92 they reach the lower third. Raising the camera from z 1.9 to 2.15 made them taller on screen.
Floor-strip saturation by frame (preview): S>0.3 share 15.0-15.5% over f48-55, 14.3% f56, 13.6% f58, 7.7% f59, 6.4% from f60 on. The collapse completes on the downbeat.
Final threshold A/B (0.01 vs 0.02) at f50/f120: mean |d| 0.41/0.21 per 255; floor high-pass noise 0.131->0.138 and 0.183->0.191; wall unchanged. About 20% faster.

rejected_critic_items: Glow-shell sphere (Add(Emission x fresnel^3, Transparent) at 2.2x the core): rejected. Lead G1 requires S01's identical compositor bloom on every orb so the protagonist light looks the same everywhere; an S05-only shell would break that.

Additive coloured cores (Add(Emission k~4, Transparent)) for the fuse: rejected. They would change the single halo definition shared with S01 and S02, and on lavender they lose their saturation. I used the critic's alternative instead: coloured halos shrink to 0.5 while W pops from inside (f57-62).

Exact restage positions O=(0,1.4,1.20), split +-1.2 m, z 1.15-1.32: adapted, not used as given. With the round-2 lockup (larger, higher title) that row gave short fans of about 40 px and a tangle. I used O=(0,2.0,0.92) with +-0.9 m, which keeps the orb row at 36% and gives longer fans. The same SPOT 100 deg / blend 0.4 aimed at (0,-0.6,0) and the neutral split are kept.

FaceKey at the suggested power with the letters' lit-body V at 0.82-0.88 and at most 20% of pixels above 0.89: not met by design. Every palette colour with a 255 channel fails a channel>0.89 test at any value above 0.89. Saturation and hue were treated as the real targets: hue met for all 10 letters, saturation for 8 of 10.

Title mean luma above the wall mean: not met. It needs a wall below ~0.6 display, which read dusky and grey and conflicts with G2. The title does beat the foreground floor (0.596 vs 0.581), and no floor block outshines the letters.

Solid tiles within 8 deg of palette hue with V >= wall V - 0.05: rejected. The lead asked for a calmer band with softer contrast, so the solid tiles are deliberately softened 40% toward the wall colour.

Cove D.mat_clay(D.mix_col('lavender','lilac',0.35)): not used as written. D.mix_col returns linear RGBA and mat_clay linearises again, which would give a saturated periwinkle. I used a 20% mix done in linear light through an sRGB helper. The lower roughness of 0.45 was also not used: the lead's soft clear coat (0.5, roughness 0.22) does that job.

Pull-back ease p^1.35: replaced by a 4-frame speed ramp. With the 5 m word, p^1.35 kept the camera so close that the L landed off-frame on its f16 hit. The ramp gives 466/452/413 px on f1-3, which still holds the circle match.
Moving the electrical swap to f61: not done. The lights are co-located from f61, so the swap is invisible either way; it stays at the storyboard's f71.
Shifting the S02 tile window to avoid its p_060->061 cut landing on the f61 downbeat: no change. The cut is on the beat grid.
Narrowing the split: kept at +-0.9 m. Narrower made the three shadows overlap into one at the letter bases.
